name: PRMS
one_liner: Psychiatrists' malpractice program with occurrence or claims-made policies and group coverage for prescriber-led practices.
short_description: Professional Risk Management Services manages The Psychiatrists' Program, medical malpractice insurance for psychiatrists and psychiatry groups, through carrier FAIRCO.
long_description: PRMS (Professional Risk Management Services) manages The Psychiatrists' Program, a medical professional liability program for psychiatrists that it has run since 1986. Policies are issued by Fair American Insurance and Reinsurance Company (FAIRCO), a New York domestic insurer that PRMS says is rated A++ (Superior) by A.M. Best; some group policies may be issued by Fair American Select Insurance Company, a Delaware surplus lines insurer. The PRMS trademarks belong to Transatlantic Holdings, Inc., a parent company of FAIRCO. Individual coverage is for solo psychiatrists without provider employees and comes in occurrence or claims-made form; PRMS waives tail costs on retirement at 55 or older after five continuous claims-made years, or after ten consecutive claims-made years, under its guidelines, and can carry forward a prior retroactive date. Licensing board matters have a separate limit up to $150,000 at no extra charge, HIPAA investigations up to $50,000, and telepsychiatry is included. Group policies need at least one psychiatrist and one other prescriber, and can cover NPs, psychologists, social workers, therapists and the entity on one policy. Residents and early-career psychiatrists get moonlighting and premium discounts. Terms vary by state and underwriting.

faqs.q: Who is the insurance carrier for PRMS?
faqs.a: Fair American Insurance and Reinsurance Company (FAIRCO), a New York insurer; some group policies may be issued by Fair American Select Insurance Company, a Delaware surplus lines insurer.
Yes, if the group has at least one practicing psychiatrist and another prescriber such as a nurse practitioner. All providers and the entity can be on one policy.

faqs.q: When does PRMS waive tail coverage?
faqs.a: On retirement at age 55 or older after five continuous years of claims-made coverage, or after ten consecutive claims-made years, subject to its guidelines.
Yes. PRMS states telepsychiatry coverage is included at no additional cost.
